In comparison to the conventional two-dimensional (area) detector, this model would simplify the complexity of motion detection, and would lead to a significant reduction in required memory length and computation time of a computer. Theoretical analysis demonstrates the model's capability to uniquely determine the magnitude and direction of the velocity of a moving object for an arbitrary direction of motion.

articleTitle: A precision densimeter which compensates for liquid viscosity
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: This paper describes a new densimeter, consisting of a compact pencil-sized density detector probe and a microprocessor-based display unit. The densimeter measures densities in the range 650–1500 kg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> to an accuracy of ±0.5 kg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, and automatically compensates for liquid viscosities up to 1 N · s/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The densimeter measures liquid density by the natural frequency of a thin-walled cylinder at the tip of the probe. The natural frequency varies with the density of the liquid the probe tip is immersed in. Viscosity of the liquid also affects the natural frequency of the cylinder immersed in it, as well as the amplitude of oscillation. The detector measures both the frequency and the Q factor at resonance, and uses this information to compensate for the effects of liquid viscosity.

articleTitle: An ultra-low drift DC chopper amplifier using MOSFET for large value of signal-source resistance
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: This paper describes an ultra-low drift, MOSFET, and dc chopper amplifier which can be used for signal-source resistance of 0.1 ∼ 10 MΩ. The sensitivity of this chopper amplifier decreases with the increase in signal-source resistance. We found that the decrease in the sensitivity is caused mainly by the drain-substrate and source-substrate capacitances in the MOSFET, and corrected the problem by the bootstrapping method. When using bootstrapping, these capacitances are reduced, and the temperature drift due to high signal-source resistance is improved. For an input signal source of 10 MΩ, the drift is reduced to one-tenth of its original value. Thus we were successful in building a dc amplifier with a temperature coefficient of within ± 10 nV/°C for a signal-source resistance of 0.1 ∼ 10 MΩ.

articleTitle: A microprocessor-based 6½-digit voltage divider
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A microprocessor-based, self-checking voltage divider of 22-bit resolution has been implemented as a 7-digit instrument. After an automated calibration process that requires no trimming of components, the divider can provide voltage-compensated transfer ratios accurate to ±0.5 ppm, typically at 10-V input and 0–10-mA output.

articleTitle: Minimization of operator-balance interactive warm-up by use of an “alter ego” heat source
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: Operator-equipment interaction is a well-known but frustrating part of many high-precision measurements. Deterioration in performance of a high-precision balance compelled testing to identify the cause of the problem and to establish effectiveness of the solution. An unexpected result of the tests was a clear characterization of a significant operator-balance thermal interaction and verification of the empirically determined warm-up requirement. The repeatability of the interactive effect inspired development of a replacement for the operator using an “alter ego” heat source.

articleTitle: Results of single- and two-dimensional audit experience with customers, an alternate map approach
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: Measurement Assurance Programs (MAP's) available from the National Bureau of Standards (NBS) are well-known methods of transferring physical and electrical values. However, where accuracy requirements are moderate it is not often practical to make use of these elegant techniques. In the broad definition sense MAP includes any technique by which the quality of measurements may be assured. Audit of measurement capability can fill the need for many lower accuracy requirements. Described are philosophies and types of audits. Also described are the results of eight years of technical audit of 11 laboratories using single- and two-dimensional length artifacts. Modifications to length audit philosophy to meet requirements of new computer-operated measuring equipment are briefly presented.

articleTitle: The development of the microwave detection of nonelectrical properties in China
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: This paper presents a brief survey of the evolution of microwave detection of nonelectrical quantities in China. In this historical review, emphasis is placed on some typical measurements, such as moisture content, thickness, velocity, temperature, etc. Remarkable progress in this field has been made in China during the past decade. However, many years may be needed to catch up with advances in other countries. The direction for further development is pointed out.

articleTitle: Measurement of interferograms perturbed by random phase fluctuations
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The measurement of interferograms which have been subjected to random phase fluctuations, as well as additive noise, is considered in the cases of (1) signals sufficiently strong to permit phase tracking, and (2) king averaging of weak signals. In the first case it is shown that averaging of the in-phase and quadrature components, in order to reduce additive noise, causes a decor rei at ion noise power which increases with averaging time T, peaks and then decreases with T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> Averaging of these components also increases the probability of ±2× ambiguities. Optimum averaging times and criteria for minimizing the likelihood of phase ambiguities are presented. The possibilities of obtaining reliable phase information from averaging times much longer than the coherence time of the fluctuations are shown.

articleTitle: Transient photoconductivity measurements of amorphous semiconductors by subnanosecond nitrogen lasers
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: Picosecond N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> lasers characterized with ultra-short pulse-width, high peak power, and simple detection installation are found very useful in diagnosing carrier behaviors of amorphous semiconductors which have low-drift mobility and a short lifetime. An impedance-matched sample holder and a fast rise-time preamplifier designed in this work provide this system with a high immunity to the background noise during the N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser discharge.

articleTitle: An optically coupled sampling system for transient electromagnetic measurements
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: An optically coupled sampling system (OCSS) for use in free-field transient electromagnetic environments was constructed. The system utilizes fiber-optic data links between a remote sampling head and a mainframe sampling oscilloscope and was designed to operate with a standard 7000-series Tektronix sampling oscilloscope. The primary goal of the research was to demonstrate the feasibility of fabricating a system with a bandwidth on the order of 1 GHz that was also suitable for packaging in scale-model structures. To this end, the remote sampling head can be packaged within a cylindrical shield, excluding power supplies, that measures 18-in length by 2-in diam. A bandwidth of 1 GHz was obtained consistently, with maximum values exceeding 2 GHz. This paper first provides a description of the measurement problem. An overview of the optically coupled sampling system is then presented, followed by a summary of system performance. Recommendations are made for further development.

articleTitle: Power-switched sample-and-hold provides accurate analog inputs for ADC in low-power system
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: This paper describes the design of a low-power, two-channel, 12-bit, data acquisition system with a conversion rate of 240 samples per second on each of the two input channels. Power switching the sample-and-hold module resulted in a power reduction of 140 mW compared with a continuously powered system. The total power consumption for the system was 102 mW. Preliminary information is given about the warm-up characteristics of a variety of operational amplifiers and a commercial sample-and-hold module; this is not available in the standard data books.

articleTitle: An overview of instrumentation and measurement in the People's Republic of China
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: THE instrumentation and measurement (I&M) field in the People's Republic of China is rather different from that in many other countries. The guideline of our government policy in every respect, including I&M, has been self-reliance. For the past 36 years, over 3000 kinds (accessories and plug-in units are excluded as instruments in our country) of electronic instruments have been put into production with almost all their components, devices, IC's, and even material produced domestically. In the recent decade, despite the fact that international cooperation and communication have been encouraged by our government's “open-door” policy, I&M has not drifted far from this deeply rooted idea of self-reliance. The reason might be that being a very broad field, I&M is influenced by too many factors. However, the importance of international cooperation has been widely realized and we are anticipating and believing in more progress in the near future. From this background, our I&M has been closely related and even dependent on domestic instrument development as well as manufacturing. This viewpoint will be highly reflected in this overview.

articleTitle: A method to electronically rotate a set of two-dimensional vectors
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: In this paper we report a method, and we describe a circuit, performing the rotation of a set of two-dimensional (2-D) vectors; an operation useful in applications using CRT or X-Y recorders. The vector (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">θ</inf> V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>) is turned through an angle Θ linearly related to control voltage V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">θ</inf> following the equation: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta = \pi \cdot {V_{\theta} \over V_{0}}.$</tex> The scale factor is 18°/V and a maximum rotation of ± 180° is obtained for V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">θ</inf> = ±V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> = ±10 V.

articleTitle: Parallel hybrid type of DC amplifier using modified magnetic modulator
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: This paper describes the design of a parallel hybrid type of dc amplifier which consists of a modified magnetic modulator and an ac-coupled amplifier. The modified magnetic modulator is very simple and highly accurate, incorporating bifilar windings for both input and output signals without a bandpass filter or selective amplifier. With this design it is possible to connect a high gain, ac amplifier in parallel without saturation because of decreased symmetrical components of the input winding of the modulator. The present dc amplifier can easily achieve high-input resistance and stabilized gain by the customary use of negative feedback. An equivalent of the input noise voltage and current of the parallel hybrid type of dc amplifier of about 5 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−8</sup> V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pp</inf>/√Hz and 3 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−9</sup> A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pp</inf>/√Hz at a range from dc to 10 KHz of the bandwidth of the system, and thermal drift of 5 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−8</sup> V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pp</inf>/°C and a long-term drift of 5 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−8</sup> V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pp</inf>/day were achieved.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave standards: An emerging need
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: Several technology surveys concerning millimeter-wave (MMW) measurement needs and capabilities have been conducted by the National Bureau of Standards (NBS), Boulder Laboratories, and others. The results of some of these studies are summarized. Current MMW standards and calibration capabilities at NBS are reviewed. The lack of national standards in certain frequency bands may lead to problems with the specification, acceptance testing, and calibration of some components and systems.

articleTitle: A nonlinear method to estimate model parameters of junction field-effect transistors
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: This paper describes a method to estimate the model parameters of junction-type field-effect transistors. The characteristics of the device under test are expressed by a nonlinear equivalent circuit with a dependent current source. To estimate all unknown parameters to specify the characteristics of the device, a measurement circuit is sequentially configured into three independent modes by a desk-top microcomputer. Raw data acquired in each measurement mode are sent to another computer to obtain a nonlinear estimation of the model parameters concurrently with data acquisition. The curves characterized by the estimated parameters are found to fit well to the original data. A newly designed jig for measurement (including relays to change the circuit mode) is developed utilizing the IEEE standard 488-bus system. In cooperation with additional measuring instruments, fully automated acquisition and estimation are made possible. Since estimated values of the parameters are stored by the multiuser, host computer with a device name, they are ready to be used for such a general purpose circuit simulation program as SPICE 2.

articleTitle: Comments on “microprocessor implementation of a fast and simultaneous amplitude and frequency detector for sinusoidal signals”
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The paper whose title is quoted above<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> contains several assumptions that do not exactly match further hardware implementation. The comments presented here intend to point out possible improvements leading towards better system performance.

articleTitle: Semiautomatic gauge block measurement assurance implementation: NBS Monograph 163 type I system
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The following paper describes a semiautomated gauge block calibration and process controlled system. This system uses a gauge block measurement assurance program as outlined in NBS Monograph 163 [1] as a guide for statistical control. Software-controlled gauge block measurements are monitored throughout a typical calibration to statistically detect out-of-control measurements. The system instructs the technician, prepares and edits files, prints from a menu a variety of calibration reports, and plots new control charts at regular intervals.

articleTitle: New high-accuracy electromagnetic measurement methods for read-write head alignment in floppy disk drives
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: This paper describes new techniques of measuring read-write head alignment that reflect a 5:1 improvement or greater over the conventional industry method of measuring the radial head spacing of double-sided diskette drives using cat's-eye diskettes. Measurement errors can be reduced further to nearly zero, based on calibrations with a laser interferometer. The new techniques are also being applied to measure and to correct for errors in “industry standard” cat's-eye diskettes; using the correction factors obtainable with these techniques, the “standard” diskettes can be used in the normal manner with greatly improved accuracies. Although these techniques were developed specifically for the 48 and 96 track-per-inch (tpi) 5.25-in floppy drives, they are applicable to any product that uses a double-sided read-write head assembly.

articleTitle: Resonance method of measurement of input impedance of any broadwall-launched discontinuity in microstrip transmission line
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A new microwave method of measuring the input impedance of any broad mall-launched discontinuity in microstrip transmission lines is suggested. In this work the reactance of a metallic post forming a broadwall-launched discontinuity in a microstrip transmission line has been characterized. An analytical expression for reactance of this metallic post has been derived considering it to be an antenna in unbounded space under appropriate boundary conditions, and considering the strip transmission line as an approximation of a planar waveguide. The proposed method is also applicable for measuring impedance of any other broad wall-launched discontinuity in microstrip transmission lines.

articleTitle: Another look at P/AR
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The P/AR rating is based on the ratio of the measured peak and full wave, rectified average values of a special test waveform. The study reported here re-examines the P/AR concept as specified by Bell Laboratories along with variant forms of that concept. The results show that in the case of the Bell implementation, poor correlation exists between P/AR ratings and bandwidth as estimated on the basis of standard filtering elements. A modified form of the test is shown to yield a P/AR value that is maximum for the unperturbed signal. The results also show that in some — but not all — cases, an improved correlation exists between P/AR rating and bandwidth for modified forms of the test.

articleTitle: Standard RF magnetic field from a rotating field generator
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: For the sensitivity testing of a radio receiver, a generator is described which has a uniform and rotating field around the test point, and makes the positioning of the receiver easier than the conventional method. The region in which the magnetic field strength is within a certain tolerance is represented as a cylindrical space. The response of a ferrite-core loop antenna located in the cylindrical space was measured, and confirmed that a receiver test is able to be carried out independently of the position and the orientation of the core antenna in the receiver.

articleTitle: Microprocessor-based system for full automation and on-line measurement of conductivity in amorphous semiconductor
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A microprocessor-based system is developed to automate measurement and to enable on-line calculation of conductivity (δ) in amorphous semiconductors [11]-[4]. The system improves the accuracy of recorded data, eliminates varying degrees of buman participation. and saves operator time. A microprocessor controls all system operalions, performs data logging and processing, and makes decisions relative to the acceptability of the measured values of the sample current and temperature (T). Results obtained and quantitative data are presented to evaluate performance characteristics of the system.

articleTitle: An instrument for the precision measurement of attenuation in a waveguide network
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A precision instrument for the continuous monitoring of the unidirectional loss in an overmoded circular waveguide communication system is described. The unit is capable of measuring an attenuation in the range 36–56 dB with an absolute accuracy of ±0.4 dB at any frequency in the range 51.85–52.05 GHz. The instrument is implemented as a switched heterodyne radiometer, which continually compares the power level received from a remote CW source via the waveguide network against power generated by a local reference source at the same frequency. The received power reference is an accurate, stable, thermocouple power meter.

articleTitle: Microcomputer-based signal processor for short range FM radar
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: This paper describes the design and testing of a microcomputer-based data acquistion and range display instrument for use with FM radar systems. The system was particularly designed to measure targets at close range (two meters or less). The instrument has been applied to the problem of measuring the bed level within a fluidized-bed combustion chamber. Results of our experiments indicate that for monitoring static targets, an average error of 2–4 percent can be expected. For the more demanding case of dynamic targets the accuracy is reduced slightly with errors on the order of 4 percent; at the same time, subjectivity is significantly increased.

articleTitle: A brief survey of the measurement of high-frequency linear network parameters in the People's Republic of China
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The development of a high-frequency linear network parameters measurement branch in the People's Republic of China is briefly summarized in this paper. The slow development in an isolated state from the mid-60's to the mid-70's is recollected. The relativey rapid progress since the late 1970's is described with references given. Recent advances, including up-to-date hardware as well as theoretical work, are presented to cover the current main achievements. Having worked in this branch and been closely contacted with certain other measurement branches for 20 years, the author hopes, even believes, this brief survey could be a sample image of the development of the whole instrumentation and measurement field in this country.

articleTitle: A device for positioning and tracking of luminous targets
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A microprocessor-controlled passive optoelectronic device for detecting and tracking luminous objects is discussed, which has accurate position determination both in azimuth and elevation. The device consists of four solid-state integrated diode arrays 100 × 100 with pin-holes as imaging dements. Signal processing provides background suppression which results in a substantial detection range extension. The device performance is discussed in terms of range and accuracy. By appropriate choice of read-out rate, the desired range and the detector response time are achieved.

articleTitle: Error analysis for dielectric spectroscopy using shielded open-circuited coaxial lines of general length
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The shielded open-circuited coaxial line of genera! length is studied in detail as a sample cell for broad-band measurements of the dielectric permittivity. This cell is a section of transmission line with the center conductor abruptly terminated. The dielectric material to be measured fills the coaxial section of the cell and extends beyond the center conductor into the tube formed by the outer conductor of the transmission line The inverse function for obtaining the permittivity of the sample from the measured input admittance of the cell is multivalued. The error in the measured permittivity caused by passing onto the wrong branch of the inverse function is analyzed, and a procedure that can prevent passage onto the wrong branch is developed. The error in the measured permittivity due to the inaccuracies in the instrumentation is also analyzed. Contour graphs are constructed that quantify the effects of this error on the measured permittivity. This error is shown to be largest when the combination of frequency, sample length, and sample permittivity place the measured normalized admittance near a branch point of the inverse function. The permittivities of several primary alcohols were measured with the open-circuited sample cell. The measured relaxation spectra for these alcohals are used to demonstrate the usefulness of the error analysis.

articleTitle: Performance comparisons of contour extraction algorithms
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: Computer analysis of video images is a popular technique for noncontact measurement and inspection. These applications frequently require the identification and extraction of the contours of areas of interest in the image from which a variety of measurements can be made including location, orientation, and shape. Recent examples include detecting flaws in hot steel slabs, measuring surface defects in wood, finding growth traces in microbiology samples, and a host of applications in the area of robotics and flexible manufacturing. Several techniques for contour extraction are surveyed; a new algorithm is described and compared with previous methods in terms of number of calculations, memory requirements, and data structures. We show that the new algorithm performs significantly faster and is more robust at the expense of a small increase in memory. Due to its sequential nature, it is suitable for on-line execution during the raster scan of a TV sensor.

articleTitle: Synthesizing signal generator for use with lock-in amplifiers in audiofrequency measurements
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: Lock-in amplifiers may be used to measure audiofrequency signals with linearity errors of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup> or less. Accuracy is often limited, however, by errors of 1–2 percent in the quadrature separation of the lock-in's polarizing signals. A signal generator is described which in the range 31 Hz–8 kHz provides sinusoidal measuring signals together with a square-wave signal which may be phase-shifted in precise steps of 90°. With this square wave as the external reference of a lock-in, signals may be resolved into orthogonal components with accuracies of 1 in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>. The generator is programmable, and so permits sequences of measurements to be executed under computer control.

articleTitle: Some experimental results from random testing of microprocessors
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A random input pattern tester for MC-6800 microprocessors is presented. The tester is based on an efficient input pattern generator which generates the inputs with the required probability distribution. Experimental results are presented. The test length, which is a function of the pattern sequence the moment a faulty output is observed corresponding to the circuit is a random variable. We illustrate the statistical properties of the test length. Comparisons are made between the deterministic and random experiments and also between the experimental and theoretical results of the random testing.

articleTitle: Survey of various Z-domain to S-domain transformations
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: The basic objective of this paper is to study the unity in diversity of the various z-domaia to s-domain transformations and find under what conditions they yield similar results. The various transformations include impulse invariant, step invariant, bilinear transformation, ramp invariant transformations, and so on. The second objective is to find out under what conditions the continuous differential equation describing the system may be approximated by a difference equation for all the various z-domaia transformations. The third objective is to find out under what assumptions the discrete version of the impulse response becomes a sampled version of the continuous response. Finally, numerical results are presented to study the degree of accuracy of various approximations as a function of the sampling rate.

articleTitle: A portable high-speed digital image processing instrument for the enhancement of television images
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: It is known that digital images may be usefully enhanced using two-dimensional (2D) recursive filters. The associated digital filter algorithms must have acceptable word lengths and be implement-able over the entire image at an acceptable processing speed. Spatial-integrator 2D filtering algorithms and recursion along diagonal lines of pixels are used to permit the design and construction of a fast, portable, and low-cost television image-enhancement instrument. Menu-driven software permits the nonspecialist user to enhance television images in less than 4 s using any of 27 different 2D filter transfer functions.

articleTitle: Measurement of RF signal generator phase noise using a one-generator delay-line method
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: A technique is described which utilizes a single generator and a delay line for the measurement of frequency-domain phase noise (£<(f)) in synthesized signal generators. Terms are defined and equations developed for theory and calculations of normalized phase-noise sideband power in a 1-Hz bandwidth offset 20 kHz from signal frequencies of interest. The system described covers the range from 0.45 to 2000 MHz. The function and contribution of each component in the measurement system is presented. Advantages of this method are discussed and a brief error analysis is given.

articleTitle: A comparison of three bandwidth measurement techniques for multimode optical fibers
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: This paper presents the results of an experiment intended to compare three distinct methods of measuring the bandwidth of a telecommunication grade, multimode optical fiber. The three methods are: 1) the time-domain method; 2) the frequency-domain method; and 3) the pulse-spectrum analysis method. We find good agreement between the frequency-domain method and the pulse-spectrum analysis method, but the time-domain method yields results that are lower than the other two for the cases we considered.

articleTitle: A bus programmable autobalancing AC/DC thermal transfer standard
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: Precision ac voltage measurements use transfer techniques which compare the rms heating value of the unknown waveform to an identical dc voltage which is readily measured. Recent developments in thermoelement technology and the development of more accurate digital ac voltmeters and ac voltage calibrators have upgraded ac measurement capability to the 80-ppm uncertainty range. NBS traceable calibration of these instruments is now possible through the development of the new IEEE 488 programmable autobalancing ac/dc transfer standard. The techniques which permit automated computer-aided ac measurements to 100 MHz with uncertainties to 30 ppm are described in this paper.

abstract: Each year the Instrument and Measurement Society appropriately recognizes the best published paper of the previous year. abstract: THE Instrumentation and Measurement Society is pleased to announce that the winner of the 1985 Andrew R. Chi Prize Paper Award is Robert D.
